children: The benchmark indices staged a stellar rally on November 19, with the Nifty 50 surging more than 1 percent to close above the 25,500 mark, supported by positive market breadth. Around 1,790 stocks advanced against 1,510 declining stocks on the NSE. However, the market may witness some profit booking and consolidation following the sharp rally from the October lows. Here are some short-term trading ideas to watch:
Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking
TVS Motor Company | CMP: Rs 4,601.4

TVS Motor Company has witnessed a strong breakout above its recent consolidation range and successfully retested the breakout zone near Rs 4,475, indicating a healthy improvement in its price structure. The stock is now approaching its all-time high, with encouraging volume participation reinforcing the strength of the ongoing uptrend.

From a technical perspective, it continues to trade comfortably above its 20-day, 50-day and 200-day EMAs, reflecting a positive alignment across the short-, medium- and long-term trends. The RSI at 66.95, firmly above the 60 mark, further highlights sustained bullish momentum.

As long as the stock sustains above the Rs 4,475 breakout zone, the positive price structure is likely to remain intact, opening up the possibility of an extended move towards Rs 5,100. The recommended stop-loss is placed at Rs 4,360.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 5,100
Stop-Loss: Rs 4,360
Quess Corp | CMP: Rs 347.2

Quess Corp has witnessed a positive move after breaking out of its descending channel pattern and successfully retesting the breakout zone with volume support. The stock has also found support near its 20-day and 50-day EMAs, lending further strength to the current price structure.

The MACD indicator is showing further improvement, with both the MACD and signal lines sustaining above the zero line, while the histogram remains in positive territory. These signals indicate that bullish momentum is gradually building.
Sustaining above the recent support zone could help the stock move towards Rs 390, with a stop-loss placed at Rs 324.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 390
Stop-Loss: Rs 324
Gabriel India | CMP: Rs 1,585.1

Gabriel India has broken out of a symmetrical triangle pattern and successfully retested the breakout zone. The stock is now sustaining above this level with healthy volume participation, indicating continued buying interest.

The Supertrend indicator is also supporting the positive trend, suggesting that bullish momentum remains intact. The RSI currently stands at 61.88, reflecting strong momentum and a favourable technical outlook.
If the stock continues to hold above its breakout level, the upward move could extend towards Rs 1,800. The recommended stop-loss is placed at Rs 1,480 to manage downside risk.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 1,800
Stop-Loss: Rs 1,480
Om Mehra, Technical Research Analyst, Samco Securities
Avenue Supermarts | CMP: Rs 3,500

Avenue Supermarts (DMart) has broken above a falling trendline on the daily chart and is emerging from a saucer pattern, signalling a meaningful improvement in its near-term trend. The stock has been recovering steadily, while its open-equal-to-low formation reflects strength from the opening tick.
The RSI has recovered sharply from oversold territory to nearly 58, while the MACD has generated a fresh bullish crossover, accompanied by an expanding histogram, indicating improving momentum.
Accordingly, traders can consider long positions at the current market price (CMP) of Rs 3,500, with an upside target of Rs 3,720 and a stop-loss at Rs 3,380.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 3,720
Stop-Loss: Rs 3,380
Mankind Pharma | CMP: Rs 2,629

Mankind Pharma has staged a sharp recovery from its recent lows and is now forming a consistent sequence of higher highs on the daily chart. The stock is trading comfortably above its 20-day SMA, placed near Rs 2,535, while all its key moving averages are trending higher.
The intraday decline to Rs 2,584 was absorbed well, with the stock closing near the day's high, reflecting resilience at higher levels.
The RSI is placed near 63 and remains firm, while the MACD continues to trade in positive territory, with the histogram expanding, indicating sustained bullish momentum.
Accordingly, traders can consider long positions at the CMP of Rs 2,629, with an upside target of Rs 2,800 and a stop-loss at Rs 2,550.
Bharat Electronics | CMP: Rs 404.2

Bharat Electronics has broken above a falling trendline on the daily chart, signalling a meaningful improvement in its near-term trend. The stock has reclaimed the Rs 400 mark and closed at the day's high, with its open-equal-to-low formation indicating strength from the opening bell.
The stock is trading comfortably above its 20-day SMA, placed near Rs 387, which continues to trend higher.
The RSI is placed near 62 and remains firm in the upper range, reflecting sustained bullish momentum.
Accordingly, traders can consider long positions at the CMP of Rs 404.20, with an upside target of Rs 430 and a stop-loss at Rs 387.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 430
Stop-Loss: Rs 387
Jay Mehta, Technical Research at JM Financial Services
Indian Railway Finance Corporation | CMP: Rs 84.26

IRFC has broken out of a double-bottom pattern around the Rs 80 level and rallied significantly towards Rs 90. Over the past six sessions, the stock retraced towards the breakout zone to retest it, found support near its 50-day EMA and has now staged a strong rebound with volume support, indicating renewed buying interest.
Momentum and trend indicators also support the prevailing bullish bias, suggesting the possibility of further upside.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 88.5, Rs 92
Stop-Loss: Rs 79.54
Pidilite Industries | CMP: Rs 1,580.5

Pidilite Industries broke out of a downward-sloping channel on November 2, around the Rs 1,460 level, and rallied significantly towards Rs 1,600. Over the last six sessions, the stock underwent a pullback and found strong support in the EMA convergence zone around Rs 1,526-1,530.
The latest trading session witnessed a strong rebound from this support zone, accompanied by healthy volume participation. Momentum and trend indicators also support the prevailing bullish bias.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 1,698, Rs 1,750
Stop-Loss: Rs 1,500
Gujarat Fluorochemicals | CMP: Rs 4,978.6

Gujarat Fluorochemicals has registered a strong breakout above its previous all-time high. The latest candle closed above this level, accompanied by robust volume participation. The breakout occurred around the Rs 4,942 mark.
On the weekly chart, the stock has also broken out of a bullish flag-and-pole continuation pattern. It is trading comfortably above its key moving averages, all of which are sloping upwards.

Trading volumes have remained consistently strong over the last six sessions, indicating healthy market participation and buying interest. Momentum and trend indicators also support the prevailing bullish bias.
Strategy: Buy
Target: Rs 5,465, Rs 5,640
Stop-Loss: Rs 4,530
